# enum_iterator - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/enum-iterator/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#overview)Overview

Tools to iterate over the values of a type.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use enum_iterator::{all, cardinality, first, last, next, previous, reverse_all, Sequence};
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Sequence)]
enum Day { Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday }
assert_eq!(cardinality::<Day>(), 7);
assert_eq!(all::<Day>().collect::<Vec<_>>(), [
    Day::Monday,
    Day::Tuesday,
    Day::Wednesday,
    Day::Thursday,
    Day::Friday,
    Day::Saturday,
    Day::Sunday,
]);
assert_eq!(first::<Day>(), Some(Day::Monday));
assert_eq!(last::<Day>(), Some(Day::Sunday));
assert_eq!(next(&Day::Tuesday), Some(Day::Wednesday));
assert_eq!(previous(&Day::Wednesday), Some(Day::Tuesday));
assert_eq!(reverse_all::<Day>().collect::<Vec<_>>(), [
    Day::Sunday,
    Day::Saturday,
    Day::Friday,
    Day::Thursday,
    Day::Wednesday,
    Day::Tuesday,
    Day::Monday,
]);
```
```
use enum_iterator::{cardinality, first, last, Sequence};
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Sequence)]
struct Foo {
    a: bool,
    b: u8,
}
assert_eq!(cardinality::<Foo>(), 512);
assert_eq!(first::<Foo>(), Some(Foo { a: false, b: 0 }));
assert_eq!(last::<Foo>(), Some(Foo { a: true, b: 255 }));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#custom-crate-path-in-generated-code)Custom crate path in generated code

The code generated by the derive macro defaults to using `::enum_iterator` as the path for
items defined in this crate. This can be customized using the
`#[enum_iterator(crate = foo::bar)]` derive macro attribute.

```
#[derive(enum_iterator::Sequence)]
#[enum_iterator(crate = enum_iterator)]
struct Foo;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#rust-version)Rust version

This crate tracks stable Rust. Minor releases may require a newer Rust version. Patch releases must not require a newer Rust version.

[§](https://docs.rs#contribute)Contribute

All contributions shall be licensed under the [0BSD license](https://spdx.org/licenses/0BSD.html).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [All](https://docs.rs/struct.All.html)
- Iterator over the values of type `T`.
- [Reverse](https://docs.rs/struct.ReverseAll.html)- All
- Iterator over the values of type `T`in reverse order.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Sequence](https://docs.rs/trait.Sequence.html)
- Trait to iterate over the values of a type.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [all](https://docs.rs/fn.all.html)
- Returns an iterator over all values of type `T`.
- [cardinality](https://docs.rs/fn.cardinality.html)
- Returns the cardinality (number of values) of `T`
- [first](https://docs.rs/fn.first.html)
- Returns the first value of type `T`.
- [last](https://docs.rs/fn.last.html)
- Returns the last value of type `T`.
- [next](https://docs.rs/fn.next.html)
- Returns the next value of type `T`or`None`if this was the end.
- [next_](https://docs.rs/fn.next_cycle.html)- cycle
- Returns the next value of type `T`or`first()`
- [previous](https://docs.rs/fn.previous.html)
- Returns the previous value of type `T`or`None`if this was the beginning.
- [previous_](https://docs.rs/fn.previous_cycle.html)- cycle
- Returns the previous value of type `T`or`last()`
- [reverse_](https://docs.rs/fn.reverse_all.html)- all
- Returns an iterator over all values of type `T`in the reverse order of`all`

## Derive Macros[§](https://docs.rs#derives)

- [Sequence](https://docs.rs/derive.Sequence.html)
- Derives `Sequence`.

# About Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/about

Docs.rs is an
            [open source](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs)
            documentation host for crates of the
            [Rust Programming Language](https://www.rust-lang.org/).
            All libraries published to [crates.io](https://crates.io)
            are documented. If you just published a crate, your crate is likely
            still in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

            The source code of Docs.rs is available on
            [GitHub](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs). If
            you ever encounter an issue, don't hesitate to report it! (And
            thanks in advance!)

Currently running Docs.rs version is: **0.0.0 (964c90a45859fd8f9076e3cbe58470a5a4f4d4f7 2026-07-01 )**

Summaries of the documentation build processes [are available at /releases/](https://docs.rs/releases).

            JavaScript in support of documentation is allowed but not guaranteed to work on docs.rs. What that
            means: If you write documentation that inlines some JavaScript (like
            [KaTeX](https://katex.org/)), that's allowed, and
            will probably work today but may break in the future.

However, it's not allowed to put JavaScript or other content in docs published on docs.rs for the purpose of tracking visitors. For instance, adding Google Analytics scripts, tracking pixels, or site verification for services like Google Search Console. Crates that do this will have the relevant versions removed and may be blocked from docs.rs.

            Docs.rs is run and maintained by the [Docs.rs team](https://www.rust-lang.org/governance/teams/dev-tools#team-docs-rs).
            You can find us in #t-docs-rs on [Zulip](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/356853-t-docs-rs).

# Builds

Source: https://docs.rs/about/builds

Docs.rs automatically builds documentation for crates released on [crates.io](https://crates.io/).
                It may take a while to build your crate, depending on how many crates are in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

                All crates are built in a sandbox using the nightly release of the Rust compiler.
                The current version in use is `rustc 1.98.0-nightly (4c9d2bfe4 2026-07-01)`.

                The README displayed on docs.rs follows Cargo’s `package.readme` rules.
                If `readme` is not set, docs.rs will look for `README.md`, `README.txt`, or `README` in the crate root.
                Set `readme = "path/to/file"` to use a custom file, `readme = true` to use `README.md`, or `readme = false` to disable the README.

                To recognize Docs.rs from your Rust code, you can test for the `docsrs` cfg, e.g.:

```
```
                To recognize Docs.rs from `build.rs` files, you can test for the environment variable `DOCS_RS`, e.g.:

`if var.is_ok `
              All targets other than `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` are cross-compiled. For implementation reasons, this is unlikely to change for the foreseeable future.

                You can configure how your crate is built by adding [package metadata](https://docs.rs/metadata) to your `Cargo.toml`, e.g.:

```
[]
 = ["--cfg", "my_cfg"]
```
`#[cfg(my_cfg)]` (not to be confused with `#[cfg(doc)]`) can be used for conditional compilation.
                This approach is also useful for setting
                When you start using docs.rs metadata or `#[cfg(docsrs)]` in your code, you might run into issues
                where your code builds fine locally but fails on docs.rs.
                To avoid this, you can add [ cargo docs-rs](https://github.com/dtolnay/cargo-docs-rs) to
                your test-suite.
                While it doesn't perfectly replicate our build environment, it can catch many common issues.

                The Docs.rs [README](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/blob/master/README.md#build-subcommand) describes how to build
                unpublished crate documentation locally using the same build environment as the Docs.rs build agent.

                Missing dependencies are a common reason for failed builds.
                Docs.rs dependencies are managed through
                [crates-build-env](https://github.com/rust-lang/crates-build-env).
                See [Forge](https://forge.rust-lang.org/docs-rs/add-dependencies.html) for how to add a dependency.

                Most of the sandbox is a read-only file system, including the source directory of your crate and its dependencies.
                If your `build.rs` generates files that are relevant for documentation, consider writing to the
                [cargo output directory](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/environment-variables.html#environment-variables-cargo-sets-for-crates),
                passed in the environment variable `OUT_DIR`.

All the builds are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The current limits are:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                If your build fails because it hit one of these limits, please
                [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                to get them increased for your crate.
                Since our build agent has finite resources, we have to consider each case individually. However, there are a few general policies:

If your crate fails to build for a reason not listed here, you can rebuild it from [crates.io](https://crates.io) website as you can see below:

Or you can [file an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues) if you think it's a **docs.rs** issue.

# Metadata

Source: https://docs.rs/about/metadata

You can customize docs.rs builds by defining `[package.metadata.docs.rs]`
		table in your crates' `Cargo.toml`.

The available configuration flags you can customize are:

```
[]
 = "test"
[]
# Features to pass to Cargo (default: [])
 = ["feature1", "feature2"]
# Whether to pass `--all-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Whether to pass `--no-default-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Target to test build on, used as the default landing page (default: "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu")
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
 = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"
# Targets to build (default: see below)
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
#
# Default targets:
# - x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - aarch64-apple-darwin
# - x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
# - aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - i686-pc-windows-msvc
#
# Set this to `[]` to only build the default target.
#
# If `default-target` is unset, the first element of `targets` is treated as the default target.
# Otherwise, these `targets` are built in addition to the default target.
# If both `default-target` and `targets` are unset,
#   all tier-one targets will be built and `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` will be used as the default target.
 = ["aarch64-apple-darwin", "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"]
# If you want to instead add another target without overwriting the default ones:
 = ["i686-apple-darwin"]
# Additional `RUSTFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustc-arg"]
# Additional `RUSTDOCFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustdoc-arg"]
# List of command line arguments for `cargo`.
#
# These cannot be a subcommand, they may only be options.
 = ["-Z", "build-std"]
```

# Shorthand URLs

Source: https://docs.rs/about/redirections

Docs.rs uses semver to parse URLs. You can use this feature to access
            crates' documentation easily. Example of URL redirections for
            `clap` crate:

| URL | Redirects to documentation of |
|---|---|
| [docs.rs/clap](https://docs.rs/clap) | Latest version of clap |
| [docs.rs/clap::Command](https://docs.rs/clap::Command) | Latest version of clap, and search for "Command" within the crate |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2) | 2.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2.9](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2.9) | 2.9.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/2.9.3](https://docs.rs/clap/2.9.3) | 2.9.3 version (you don't need `=`unlike semver) |
| [docs.rs/clap/*](https://docs.rs/clap/*) | Latest version of this page (if it still exists). "latest" or "newest" work as well as `*`. |

---

# Download

Source: https://docs.rs/about/download

docs.rs stores the `rustdoc` output in a ZIP file.

                These archives can be used as a base for further processing of
                the documentation for offline readers like Dash or Zeal.
                **They are not directly usable for offline documentation.**

The download is possible for specific or semantic versions:

But also viaTo unpack the ZIP file you need any zip utility that supports PKZIP version 4.6 and BZIP2 & Deflate compression.

The archives will contain all the documentation HTML files for all targets and CSS/JS assets that are specific to the build. The default target will be found at the root, and other targets each in its own subfolder.

                Docs.rs is running rustdoc with `--static-root-path "/-/rustdoc.static/"`,
                which leads to all references to static assets breaking if they are not
                available under that path. Older builds used `--static-root-path "/"`, which
                means you will have to handle both.

                Since we're also adding `--emit=invocation-specific` to our build
                the archives will *not* contain any static assets that are specific to the
                toolchain. For now these will have to be downloaded file-by-file directly
                from docs.rs.

---

# Rustdoc JSON

Source: https://docs.rs/about/rustdoc-json

docs.rs builds & hosts the [ rustdoc JSON](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustdoc/unstable-features.html#json-output) output.

This structured version of the documentation can be used for inspecting the docs and types of the crate in a programmatic way.

                The JSON file you're downloading might have been built with an older version of `rustdoc`
                so you might have to check the `format_version` attribute to determine how to parse the structure.
                The [ rustdoc-types](https://docs.rs/rustdoc-types/) crate helps with this.

**
                We started building rustdoc JSON on 2025-05-23. So any release before that won't have a download
                available until our rebuilds reached that release.
            **

                The download URLs can be generic or specific, depending on what you need. In case of rebuilds we
                also keep old format versions around. **Until we rebuilt all releases, we might return
                a `404 NOT FOUND` for some.**

By default we use `zstd` compression, which is more space efficient and faster to decompress. For more limited environments we also started supporting `gzip` compression. You can receive gzip by adding `.gz` to the given URL.

Here some URL examples you can use.

| URL | Redirects to JSON download of |
|---|---|
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json) | latest version, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz) | latest version, default target, latest format-version, gzip compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42) | latest version, default target, format-version 42 |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json.zst](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json.zst) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version, zstd compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json) | latest version, windows target, latest format-version |

# enum_iterator - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/enum-iterator

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#overview)Overview

Tools to iterate over the values of a type.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use enum_iterator::{all, cardinality, first, last, next, previous, reverse_all, Sequence};
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Sequence)]
enum Day { Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday }
assert_eq!(cardinality::<Day>(), 7);
assert_eq!(all::<Day>().collect::<Vec<_>>(), [
    Day::Monday,
    Day::Tuesday,
    Day::Wednesday,
    Day::Thursday,
    Day::Friday,
    Day::Saturday,
    Day::Sunday,
]);
assert_eq!(first::<Day>(), Some(Day::Monday));
assert_eq!(last::<Day>(), Some(Day::Sunday));
assert_eq!(next(&Day::Tuesday), Some(Day::Wednesday));
assert_eq!(previous(&Day::Wednesday), Some(Day::Tuesday));
assert_eq!(reverse_all::<Day>().collect::<Vec<_>>(), [
    Day::Sunday,
    Day::Saturday,
    Day::Friday,
    Day::Thursday,
    Day::Wednesday,
    Day::Tuesday,
    Day::Monday,
]);
```
```
use enum_iterator::{cardinality, first, last, Sequence};
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Sequence)]
struct Foo {
    a: bool,
    b: u8,
}
assert_eq!(cardinality::<Foo>(), 512);
assert_eq!(first::<Foo>(), Some(Foo { a: false, b: 0 }));
assert_eq!(last::<Foo>(), Some(Foo { a: true, b: 255 }));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#custom-crate-path-in-generated-code)Custom crate path in generated code

The code generated by the derive macro defaults to using `::enum_iterator` as the path for
items defined in this crate. This can be customized using the
`#[enum_iterator(crate = foo::bar)]` derive macro attribute.

```
#[derive(enum_iterator::Sequence)]
#[enum_iterator(crate = enum_iterator)]
struct Foo;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#rust-version)Rust version

This crate tracks stable Rust. Minor releases may require a newer Rust version. Patch releases must not require a newer Rust version.

[§](https://docs.rs#contribute)Contribute

All contributions shall be licensed under the [0BSD license](https://spdx.org/licenses/0BSD.html).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [All](https://docs.rs/struct.All.html)
- Iterator over the values of type `T`.
- [Reverse](https://docs.rs/struct.ReverseAll.html)- All
- Iterator over the values of type `T`in reverse order.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Sequence](https://docs.rs/trait.Sequence.html)
- Trait to iterate over the values of a type.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [all](https://docs.rs/fn.all.html)
- Returns an iterator over all values of type `T`.
- [cardinality](https://docs.rs/fn.cardinality.html)
- Returns the cardinality (number of values) of `T`
- [first](https://docs.rs/fn.first.html)
- Returns the first value of type `T`.
- [last](https://docs.rs/fn.last.html)
- Returns the last value of type `T`.
- [next](https://docs.rs/fn.next.html)
- Returns the next value of type `T`or`None`if this was the end.
- [next_](https://docs.rs/fn.next_cycle.html)- cycle
- Returns the next value of type `T`or`first()`
- [previous](https://docs.rs/fn.previous.html)
- Returns the previous value of type `T`or`None`if this was the beginning.
- [previous_](https://docs.rs/fn.previous_cycle.html)- cycle
- Returns the previous value of type `T`or`last()`
- [reverse_](https://docs.rs/fn.reverse_all.html)- all
- Returns an iterator over all values of type `T`in the reverse order of`all`

## Derive Macros[§](https://docs.rs#derives)

- [Sequence](https://docs.rs/derive.Sequence.html)
- Derives `Sequence`.

# guise - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/guise-ui/0.4.0/guise/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#guise)guise

A Mantine-inspired component library for [gpui](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed).

`guise` provides a themed palette, sizing tokens, and a growing set of
ready-to-use components built on gpui’s `RenderOnce` builder pattern.

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use guise::prelude::*;
Stack::new().gap(Size::Md).child(
    Button::new("save", "Save").variant(Variant::Filled),
)
```
Install a [ Theme](https://docs.rs/theme/struct.Theme.html) once at startup, then read it from any component:

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [chart](https://docs.rs/chart/index.html)
- Charts — minimal, axis-free data visuals painted through gpui’s `canvas`.
- [data](https://docs.rs/data/index.html)
- Data display: components that present structured content.
- [editor](https://docs.rs/editor/index.html)
- Multiline text-editor building blocks.
- [feedback](https://docs.rs/feedback/index.html)
- Feedback: components that communicate state to the user.
- [flex](https://docs.rs/flex/index.html)
- Flexbox layout primitives, for people who think in `Row`/`Column`/`Container`/`Expanded`(à la Flutter).
- [input](https://docs.rs/input/index.html)
- Form inputs.
- [layout](https://docs.rs/layout/index.html)
- Layout primitives: vertical `Stack``Group``Center``AppShell``Container``Space`
- [nav](https://docs.rs/nav/index.html)
- Navigation: components for moving around an app, plus a `StatusBar`
- [overlay](https://docs.rs/overlay/index.html)
- Overlays: floating UI that paints above the page.
- [panegroup](https://docs.rs/panegroup/index.html)
- `PaneGroup`— a recursive tree of- **tabbed**panes (splits contain tabs), the Zed / VS Code editor-group workspace model as a reusable gpui component.
- [prelude](https://docs.rs/prelude/index.html)
- Common imports for building with `guise`.
- [reactive](https://docs.rs/reactive/index.html)
- A lightweight, React-flavored state layer over gpui.
- [style](https://docs.rs/style/index.html)
- Shared visual variants. Mantine resolves a `(color, variant)`pair into a background / foreground / border triple that every interactive component (Button, Badge, ActionIcon, …) draws from. This is that resolver.
- [theme](https://docs.rs/theme/index.html)
- The theme: palette + sizing tokens + color scheme, exposed as a gpui
`Global`so any component can resolve themed values during render.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Icon](https://docs.rs/enum.IconName.html)- Name
- A named icon. The glyph is resolved by `IconName::glyph`
- [Object](https://docs.rs/enum.ObjectFit.html)- Fit
- How to fit the image into the bounds of the element.
- [Orientation](https://docs.rs/enum.Orientation.html)
- [Split](https://docs.rs/enum.SplitDirection.html)- Direction
- Which way the panes are laid out. `Horizontal`places them side by side (a vertical divider, column-resize cursor);`Vertical`stacks them.
- [Split](https://docs.rs/enum.SplitPanelEvent.html)- Panel - Event
- Emitted while the divider is dragged. Carries the new first-pane ratio
in `0.0..=1.0`.
- [Transition](https://docs.rs/enum.TransitionKind.html)- Kind
- The kind of entrance motion `Transition`
- [WebView](https://docs.rs/enum.WebViewEvent.html)- Event
- Emitted as the embedded page loads and changes.

# scrin - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/scrin/0.1.83/scrin/

## Expand description

Scrin is a Rust terminal UI toolkit for building polished command-line interfaces without depending on Ratatui.

It provides a Scrin-native rendering model with buffers, colors, rectangles,
layout constraints, styled text, widgets, interaction metadata, panes,
overlays, command palettes, status bars, input routing, terminal lifecycle
helpers, and animation glue.
The effects layer is powered by [ aisling](https://crates.io/crates/aisling)
and adapts Aisling frames into Scrin buffers, so loaders and text effects can
be composed with normal Scrin widgets.

[§](https://docs.rs#install)Install

```
[dependencies]
scrin = "0.1.83"
```
[§](https://docs.rs#draw-a-widget)Draw A Widget

```
use scrin::core::buffer::Buffer;
use scrin::core::color::Color;
use scrin::core::rect::Rect;
use scrin::style::Style;
use scrin::widgets::block::Block;
use scrin::widgets::Widget;
let mut buffer = Buffer::new(40, 8);
buffer.fill(Rect::new(0, 0, 40, 8), ' ', Color::WHITE, None);
let block = Block::bordered()
    .title("scrin")
    .border_style(Style::new().fg(Color::CYAN));
block.render(&mut buffer, Rect::new(0, 0, 40, 8));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#render-an-aisling-effect-into-a-scrin-buffer)Render An Aisling Effect Into A Scrin Buffer

```
use scrin::core::{buffer::Buffer, rect::Rect};
use scrin::effects::{EffectKind, EffectPlayer};
let mut buffer = Buffer::new(60, 6);
let mut effect = EffectPlayer::new(EffectKind::Matrix, "Scrin + Aisling")
    .with_size(60, 6)
    .with_duration(24);
effect.render_to_buffer(&mut buffer, Rect::new(0, 0, 60, 6));
effect.advance();
```
[§](https://docs.rs#render-an-aisling-loader)Render An Aisling Loader

```
use scrin::core::{buffer::Buffer, rect::Rect};
use scrin::effects::{LoaderKind, LoaderPlayer};
let mut buffer = Buffer::new(48, 4);
let loader = LoaderPlayer::new(LoaderKind::Bar)
    .with_size(48, 4)
    .with_label("indexing".to_string());
let progress = LoaderPlayer::progress_from_fraction(0.42);
loader.render(3, progress, &mut buffer, Rect::new(0, 0, 48, 4));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#terminal-rendering)Terminal Rendering

[ Terminal::draw](https://docs.rs/terminal/struct.Terminal.html#method.draw) uses Scrin’s diff presenter and updates only changed
cells.

[is available when an application wants a full buffer repaint every frame, for example during dense animation.](https://docs.rs/terminal/struct.Terminal.html#method.draw_full)

Common Aisling selector/config types are re-exported from [ effects](https://docs.rs/effects/index.html) so a
Scrin application can choose effects and loaders through one crate path.

# heddle-cli

The `heddle` binary — Heddle's foreground command-line interface.

For the full Heddle product overview, install instructions, and getting started guide,
see [the workspace README](https://docs.rs/README.md). This file documents verbs whose
implementation details are too specific to belong in the product-level
README.

## Stack workflow

A *stack* is the descendant tree of related threads formed by walking
`ThreadRecord::parent_thread` links. The model lives in
[ repo::thread_stack](https://docs.rs/repo/src/thread_stack.rs); the value-type
projection used by tooling lives in

[.](https://docs.rs/repo/src/stack_snapshot.rs)

`repo::stack_snapshot`### Current surface

The stack model is an internal projection over thread records. User-facing
inspection lives on `heddle thread list` and `heddle thread show`; the removed
top-level stack verb is intentionally not part of the public CLI surface.

### Next-action verdicts

The stack next-action resolver walks the stack and emits exactly one of four verdicts. The rules:

- `blocked by <thread>`- `state = Blocked`. Blocked wins over everything; the operator must unblock before progress.
- `ready`- `Ready`,- `Merged`,- `Promoted`, or- `Abandoned`. The whole stack is shippable.
- `waiting-on-review (<thread>)`- `Active`or- `Draft`. The deepest in-flight thread is reported as the bottleneck.
- `unknown`

### JSON shape

The `RepositorySnapshot` projection uses this shape (additive fields may be added
without bumping `version`; non-additive changes bump it):

```
{
  "version": 1,
  "captured_at": "2026-05-23T17:08:00Z",
  "stacks": [
    {
      "root": {
        "name": "feature-a",
        "children": [{ "name": "feature-b", "children": [] }]
      }
    }
  ],
  "threads": [
    {
      "thread": "feature-a",
      "parent_thread": null,
      "base_state": "hd-…",
      "current_state": "hd-…",
      "state": "active",
      "freshness": "current"
    }
  ]
}
```
### Agentic harness integration

The Claude Code `PreToolUse` hook reads the snapshot and appends a stack
summary to `additionalContext` whenever the current thread is part of a
multi-member stack. Single-thread stacks add no signal worth burning
context on and are skipped. See
[ harness/claude_hook.rs](https://docs.rs/src/harness/claude_hook.rs) for the

`format_stack_context` rendering.

# odcs - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/odcs/0.5.0/odcs/

## Expand description

Reference implementation of the Open Data Contract Standard (ODCS).

[ SPEC.md](https://docs.rs/SPEC.md) at the repository root defines the upstream specification
policy. This crate implements the foundational pipeline:

`ODCS Document → Parser → Canonical Object Model → Validator → Diagnostics`[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use odcs::{parse, validate, DocumentFormat};
let yaml = br#"
version: "1.0.0"
apiVersion: "v3.1.0"
kind: "DataContract"
id: "example"
status: "draft"
"#;
let result = parse(yaml, DocumentFormat::Yaml);
let contract = result.contract.expect("parse succeeded");
let report = validate(&contract);
assert!(report.is_valid());
```

# enum_iterator - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/enum-iterator/2.3.0/target-redirect/enum_iterator/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#overview)Overview

Tools to iterate over the values of a type.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use enum_iterator::{all, cardinality, first, last, next, previous, reverse_all, Sequence};
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Sequence)]
enum Day { Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday }
assert_eq!(cardinality::<Day>(), 7);
assert_eq!(all::<Day>().collect::<Vec<_>>(), [
    Day::Monday,
    Day::Tuesday,
    Day::Wednesday,
    Day::Thursday,
    Day::Friday,
    Day::Saturday,
    Day::Sunday,
]);
assert_eq!(first::<Day>(), Some(Day::Monday));
assert_eq!(last::<Day>(), Some(Day::Sunday));
assert_eq!(next(&Day::Tuesday), Some(Day::Wednesday));
assert_eq!(previous(&Day::Wednesday), Some(Day::Tuesday));
assert_eq!(reverse_all::<Day>().collect::<Vec<_>>(), [
    Day::Sunday,
    Day::Saturday,
    Day::Friday,
    Day::Thursday,
    Day::Wednesday,
    Day::Tuesday,
    Day::Monday,
]);
```
```
use enum_iterator::{cardinality, first, last, Sequence};
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Sequence)]
struct Foo {
    a: bool,
    b: u8,
}
assert_eq!(cardinality::<Foo>(), 512);
assert_eq!(first::<Foo>(), Some(Foo { a: false, b: 0 }));
assert_eq!(last::<Foo>(), Some(Foo { a: true, b: 255 }));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#custom-crate-path-in-generated-code)Custom crate path in generated code

The code generated by the derive macro defaults to using `::enum_iterator` as the path for
items defined in this crate. This can be customized using the
`#[enum_iterator(crate = foo::bar)]` derive macro attribute.

```
#[derive(enum_iterator::Sequence)]
#[enum_iterator(crate = enum_iterator)]
struct Foo;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#rust-version)Rust version

This crate tracks stable Rust. Minor releases may require a newer Rust version. Patch releases must not require a newer Rust version.

[§](https://docs.rs#contribute)Contribute

All contributions shall be licensed under the [0BSD license](https://spdx.org/licenses/0BSD.html).

[248](https://docs.rs#248)    fn next(&mut self) -> Option<T> {

[250](https://docs.rs#250)        self.0 = item.next();
[251](https://docs.rs#251)        Some(item)
[252](https://docs.rs#252)    }
[253](https://docs.rs#253)}
[254](https://docs.rs#254)
[255](https://docs.rs#255)impl<T: Sequence> FusedIterator for All<T> {}

[274](https://docs.rs#274)
[275](https://docs.rs#275)/// Trait to iterate over the values of a type.
[276](https://docs.rs#276)///
[277](https://docs.rs#277)/// The [crate root](crate) defines useful functions to work with types implementing `Sequence`.
[278](https://docs.rs#278)///
[279](https://docs.rs#279)/// # Derivation
[280](https://docs.rs#280)///
[281](https://docs.rs#281)/// `Sequence` can be derived for `enum` and `struct` types. Specifically, it can be derived
[282](https://docs.rs#282)/// for:
[283](https://docs.rs#283)/// - Enumerations whose variants meet one of the following criteria:
[284](https://docs.rs#284)///   - The variant does not have fields.
[285](https://docs.rs#285)///   - The variant has fields meeting all these conditions:
[286](https://docs.rs#286)///     - Every field has a type that implements `Sequence`.
[287](https://docs.rs#287)///     - Every field but the last one has a type that implements `Clone`.
[288](https://docs.rs#288)/// - Enumerations without variants.
[289](https://docs.rs#289)/// - Structures whose fields meet all these conditions:
[290](https://docs.rs#290)///     - Every field has a type that implements `Sequence`.
[291](https://docs.rs#291)///     - Every field but the last one has a type that implements `Clone`.
[292](https://docs.rs#292)/// - Unit structures (i.e. without fields).
[293](https://docs.rs#293)///
[294](https://docs.rs#294)/// The cardinality (number of values) of the type must not exceed `usize::MAX`.
[295](https://docs.rs#295)///
[296](https://docs.rs#296)/// # Laws
[297](https://docs.rs#297)///
[298](https://docs.rs#298)/// `T: Sequence` implies the following assertions:
[299](https://docs.rs#299)/// - `T::first().and_then(|x| x.previous()).is_none()`
[300](https://docs.rs#300)/// - `T::last().and_then(|x| x.next()).is_none()`
[301](https://docs.rs#301)/// - `T::first().is_none()` ⇔ `T::last().is_none()`
[302](https://docs.rs#302)/// - `std::iter::successors(T::first(), T::next)` must eventually yield `T::last()`.
[303](https://docs.rs#303)/// - If `T` is inhabited, `T::first().is_some()`.
[304](https://docs.rs#304)///
[305](https://docs.rs#305)/// If a manual implementation of `Sequence` violates any of these laws, the functions at the crate root may misbehave, including panicking.
[306](https://docs.rs#306)///
[307](https://docs.rs#307)/// # Examples
[308](https://docs.rs#308)/// ## C-like enumeration
[309](https://docs.rs#309)///
[310](https://docs.rs#310)/// ```
[311](https://docs.rs#311)/// use enum_iterator::{all, cardinality, Sequence};
[312](https://docs.rs#312)///
[313](https://docs.rs#313)/// #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Sequence)]
[314](https://docs.rs#314)/// enum Direction { North, South, West, East }
[315](https://docs.rs#315)///
[316](https://docs.rs#316)/// assert_eq!(cardinality::<Direction>(), 4);
[317](https://docs.rs#317)/// assert_eq!(all::<Direction>().collect::<Vec<_>>(), [
[318](https://docs.rs#318)///     Direction::North,
[319](https://docs.rs#319)///     Direction::South,
[320](https://docs.rs#320)///     Direction::West,
[321](https://docs.rs#321)///     Direction::East,
[322](https://docs.rs#322)/// ]);
[323](https://docs.rs#323)/// ```
[324](https://docs.rs#324)///
[325](https://docs.rs#325)/// ## Enumeration with data
[326](https://docs.rs#326)///
[327](https://docs.rs#327)/// ```
[328](https://docs.rs#328)/// use enum_iterator::{all, cardinality, Sequence};
[329](https://docs.rs#329)///
[330](https://docs.rs#330)/// #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Sequence)]
[331](https://docs.rs#331)/// enum Direction { North, South, West, East }
[332](https://docs.rs#332)///
[333](https://docs.rs#333)/// #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Sequence)]
[334](https://docs.rs#334)/// enum Greeting {
[335](https://docs.rs#335)///     Hi,
[336](https://docs.rs#336)///     Bye,
[337](https://docs.rs#337)/// }
[338](https://docs.rs#338)///
[339](https://docs.rs#339)/// #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Sequence)]
[340](https://docs.rs#340)/// enum Action {
[341](https://docs.rs#341)///     Move(Direction),
[342](https://docs.rs#342)///     Jump,
[343](https://docs.rs#343)///     Talk { greeting: Greeting, loud: bool },
[344](https://docs.rs#344)/// }
[345](https://docs.rs#345)///
[346](https://docs.rs#346)/// assert_eq!(cardinality::<Action>(), 4 + 1 + 2 * 2);
[347](https://docs.rs#347)/// assert_eq!(all::<Action>().collect::<Vec<_>>(), [
[348](https://docs.rs#348)///     Action::Move(Direction::North),
[349](https://docs.rs#349)///     Action::Move(Direction::South),
[350](https://docs.rs#350)///     Action::Move(Direction::West),
[351](https://docs.rs#351)///     Action::Move(Direction::East),
[352](https://docs.rs#352)///     Action::Jump,
[353](https://docs.rs#353)///     Action::Talk { greeting: Greeting::Hi, loud: false },
[354](https://docs.rs#354)///     Action::Talk { greeting: Greeting::Hi, loud: true },
[355](https://docs.rs#355)///     Action::Talk { greeting: Greeting::Bye, loud: false },
[356](https://docs.rs#356)///     Action::Talk { greeting: Greeting::Bye, loud: true },
[357](https://docs.rs#357)/// ]);
[358](https://docs.rs#358)/// ```
[359](https://docs.rs#359)///
[360](https://docs.rs#360)/// ## Structure
[361](https://docs.rs#361)///
[362](https://docs.rs#362)/// ```
[363](https://docs.rs#363)/// use enum_iterator::{all, cardinality, Sequence};
[364](https://docs.rs#364)///
[365](https://docs.rs#365)/// #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Sequence)]
[366](https://docs.rs#366)/// enum Side {
[367](https://docs.rs#367)///     Left,
[368](https://docs.rs#368)///     Right,
[369](https://docs.rs#369)/// }
[370](https://docs.rs#370)///
[371](https://docs.rs#371)/// #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Sequence)]
[372](https://docs.rs#372)/// enum LimbKind {
[373](https://docs.rs#373)///     Arm,
[374](https://docs.rs#374)///     Leg,
[375](https://docs.rs#375)/// }
[376](https://docs.rs#376)///
[377](https://docs.rs#377)/// #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Sequence)]
[378](https://docs.rs#378)/// struct Limb {
[379](https://docs.rs#379)///     kind: LimbKind,
[380](https://docs.rs#380)///     side: Side,
[381](https://docs.rs#381)/// }
[382](https://docs.rs#382)///
[383](https://docs.rs#383)/// assert_eq!(cardinality::<Limb>(), 4);
[384](https://docs.rs#384)/// assert_eq!(all::<Limb>().collect::<Vec<_>>(), [
[385](https://docs.rs#385)///     Limb { kind: LimbKind::Arm, side: Side::Left },
[386](https://docs.rs#386)///     Limb { kind: LimbKind::Arm, side: Side::Right },
[387](https://docs.rs#387)///     Limb { kind: LimbKind::Leg, side: Side::Left },
[388](https://docs.rs#388)///     Limb { kind: LimbKind::Leg, side: Side::Right },
[389](https://docs.rs#389)/// ]);
[390](https://docs.rs#390)/// ```
[391](https://docs.rs#391)pub trait Sequence: Sized {
[392](https://docs.rs#392)    /// Number of values of type `Self`.
[393](https://docs.rs#393)    ///
[394](https://docs.rs#394)    /// # Example
[395](https://docs.rs#395)    /// ```
[396](https://docs.rs#396)    /// use enum_iterator::Sequence;
[397](https://docs.rs#397)    ///
[398](https://docs.rs#398)    /// #[derive(Sequence)]
[399](https://docs.rs#399)    /// enum Day { Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday }
[400](https://docs.rs#400)    ///
[401](https://docs.rs#401)    /// assert_eq!(Day::CARDINALITY, 7);
[402](https://docs.rs#402)    /// ```
[403](https://docs.rs#403)    const CARDINALITY: usize;
[404](https://docs.rs#404)
[405](https://docs.rs#405)    /// Returns value following `*self` or `None` if this was the end.
[406](https://docs.rs#406)    ///
[407](https://docs.rs#407)    /// Values are yielded in the following order. Comparisons between values are based on their
[408](https://docs.rs#408)    /// relative order as yielded by `next`; an element yielded after another is considered greater.
[409](https://docs.rs#409)    ///
[410](https://docs.rs#410)    /// - For primitive types, in increasing order (same as `Ord`).
[411](https://docs.rs#411)    /// - For arrays and tuples, in lexicographic order of the sequence of their elements.
[412](https://docs.rs#412)    /// - When derived for an enumeration, in variant definition order.
[413](https://docs.rs#413)    /// - When derived for a structure, in lexicographic order of the sequence of its fields taken
[414](https://docs.rs#414)    ///   in definition order.
[415](https://docs.rs#415)    ///
[416](https://docs.rs#416)    /// The order described above is the same as `Ord` if any custom `Sequence` implementation
[417](https://docs.rs#417)    /// follows `Ord` and any enumeration has its variants defined in increasing order of
[418](https://docs.rs#418)    /// discriminant.
[419](https://docs.rs#419)    ///
[420](https://docs.rs#420)    /// # Example
[421](https://docs.rs#421)    /// ```
[422](https://docs.rs#422)    /// use enum_iterator::Sequence;
[423](https://docs.rs#423)    ///
[424](https://docs.rs#424)    /// #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Sequence)]
[425](https://docs.rs#425)    /// enum Day { Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday }
[426](https://docs.rs#426)    ///
[427](https://docs.rs#427)    /// assert_eq!(Day::Tuesday.next(), Some(Day::Wednesday));
[428](https://docs.rs#428)    /// ```
[429](https://docs.rs#429)    fn next(&self) -> Option<Self>;
[430](https://docs.rs#430)
[431](https://docs.rs#431)    /// Returns value preceding `*self` or `None` if this was the beginning.
[432](https://docs.rs#432)    ///
[433](https://docs.rs#433)    /// # Example
[434](https://docs.rs#434)    /// ```
[435](https://docs.rs#435)    /// use enum_iterator::Sequence;
[436](https://docs.rs#436)    ///
[437](https://docs.rs#437)    /// #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Sequence)]
[438](https://docs.rs#438)    /// enum Day { Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday }
[439](https://docs.rs#439)    ///
[440](https://docs.rs#440)    /// assert_eq!(Day::Wednesday.previous(), Some(Day::Tuesday));
[441](https://docs.rs#441)    /// ```
[442](https://docs.rs#442)    fn previous(&self) -> Option<Self>;
[443](https://docs.rs#443)
[444](https://docs.rs#444)    /// Returns the first value of type `Self`.
[445](https://docs.rs#445)    ///
[446](https://docs.rs#446)    /// # Example
[447](https://docs.rs#447)    /// ```
[448](https://docs.rs#448)    /// use enum_iterator::Sequence;
[449](https://docs.rs#449)    ///
[450](https://docs.rs#450)    /// #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Sequence)]
[451](https://docs.rs#451)    /// enum Day { Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday }
[452](https://docs.rs#452)    ///
[453](https://docs.rs#453)    /// assert_eq!(Day::first(), Some(Day::Monday));
[454](https://docs.rs#454)    /// ```
[455](https://docs.rs#455)    fn first() -> Option<Self>;
[456](https://docs.rs#456)
[457](https://docs.rs#457)    /// Returns the last value of type `Self`.
[458](https://docs.rs#458)    ///
[459](https://docs.rs#459)    /// # Example
[460](https://docs.rs#460)    /// ```
[461](https://docs.rs#461)    /// use enum_iterator::Sequence;
[462](https://docs.rs#462)    ///
[463](https://docs.rs#463)    /// #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Sequence)]
[464](https://docs.rs#464)    /// enum Day { Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday }
[465](https://docs.rs#465)    ///
[466](https://docs.rs#466)    /// assert_eq!(Day::last(), Some(Day::Sunday));
[467](https://docs.rs#467)    /// ```
[468](https://docs.rs#468)    fn last() -> Option<Self>;
[469](https://docs.rs#469)}
[470](https://docs.rs#470)

[612](https://docs.rs#612)impl<T: Sequence> Sequence for Poll<T> {

[616](https://docs.rs#616)        match self {
[617](https://docs.rs#617)            Poll::Ready(x) => x.next().map(Poll::Ready).or(Some(Poll::Pending)),
[618](https://docs.rs#618)            Poll::Pending => None,
[619](https://docs.rs#619)        }
[620](https://docs.rs#620)    }

[625](https://docs.rs#625)            Poll::Pending => T::last().map(Poll::Ready),
[626](https://docs.rs#626)        }

[629](https://docs.rs#629)    fn first() -> Option<Self> {

[631](https://docs.rs#631)    }

[633](https://docs.rs#633)    fn last() -> Option<Self> {
[634](https://docs.rs#634)        Some(Poll::Pending)

[637](https://docs.rs#637)
[638](https://docs.rs#638)impl<const N: usize, T: Sequence + Clone> Sequence for [T; N] {
[639](https://docs.rs#639)    const CARDINALITY: usize = {
[640](https://docs.rs#640)        let tc = T::CARDINALITY;
[641](https://docs.rs#641)        let mut c = 1;
[642](https://docs.rs#642)        let mut i = 0;
[643](https://docs.rs#643)        loop {
[644](https://docs.rs#644)            if i == N {
[645](https://docs.rs#645)                break c;
[646](https://docs.rs#646)            }
[647](https://docs.rs#647)            c *= tc;
[648](https://docs.rs#648)            i += 1;
[649](https://docs.rs#649)        }
[650](https://docs.rs#650)    };
[651](https://docs.rs#651)
[652](https://docs.rs#652)    fn next(&self) -> Option<Self> {
[653](https://docs.rs#653)        advance_for_array(self, T::first)
[654](https://docs.rs#654)    }
[655](https://docs.rs#655)
[656](https://docs.rs#656)    fn previous(&self) -> Option<Self> {
[657](https://docs.rs#657)        advance_for_array(self, T::last)
[658](https://docs.rs#658)    }
[659](https://docs.rs#659)
[660](https://docs.rs#660)    fn first() -> Option<Self> {
[661](https://docs.rs#661)        if N == 0 {
[662](https://docs.rs#662)            Some(core::array::from_fn(|_| unreachable!()))
[663](https://docs.rs#663)        } else {
[664](https://docs.rs#664)            let x = T::first()?;
[665](https://docs.rs#665)            Some(core::array::from_fn(|_| x.clone()))
[666](https://docs.rs#666)        }
[667](https://docs.rs#667)    }
[668](https://docs.rs#668)
[669](https://docs.rs#669)    fn last() -> Option<Self> {
[670](https://docs.rs#670)        if N == 0 {
[671](https://docs.rs#671)            Some(core::array::from_fn(|_| unreachable!()))
[672](https://docs.rs#672)        } else {
[673](https://docs.rs#673)            let x = T::last()?;
[674](https://docs.rs#674)            Some(core::array::from_fn(|_| x.clone()))
[675](https://docs.rs#675)        }
[676](https://docs.rs#676)    }
[677](https://docs.rs#677)}
[678](https://docs.rs#678)
[679](https://docs.rs#679)fn advance_for_array<const N: usize, T, R>(a: &[T; N], reset: R) -> Option<[T; N]>
[680](https://docs.rs#680)where
[681](https://docs.rs#681)    T: Sequence + Clone,
[682](https://docs.rs#682)    R: Fn() -> Option<T>,
[683](https://docs.rs#683){
[684](https://docs.rs#684)    let mut a = a.clone();
[685](https://docs.rs#685)    let keep = a.iter_mut().rev().try_fold((), |_, x| match x.next() {
[686](https://docs.rs#686)        Some(new_x) => {
[687](https://docs.rs#687)            *x = new_x;
[688](https://docs.rs#688)            ControlFlow::Break(true)
[689](https://docs.rs#689)        }
[690](https://docs.rs#690)        None => match reset() {
[691](https://docs.rs#691)            Some(new_x) => {
[692](https://docs.rs#692)                *x = new_x;
[693](https://docs.rs#693)                ControlFlow::Continue(())
[694](https://docs.rs#694)            }
[695](https://docs.rs#695)            None => ControlFlow::Break(false),
[696](https://docs.rs#696)        },
[697](https://docs.rs#697)    });
[698](https://docs.rs#698)    Some(a).filter(|_| matches!(keep, ControlFlow::Break(true)))
[699](https://docs.rs#699)}

[701](https://docs.rs#701)macro_rules! impl_seq_advance_for_tuple {
[702](https://docs.rs#702)    (
[703](https://docs.rs#703)        $this:ident,
[704](https://docs.rs#704)        $advance:ident,
[705](https://docs.rs#705)        $reset:ident,
[706](https://docs.rs#706)        $carry:ident
[707](https://docs.rs#707)        @ $($values:expr,)*
[708](https://docs.rs#708)        @
[709](https://docs.rs#709)        @ $($placeholders:pat,)*
[710](https://docs.rs#710)    ) => {
[711](https://docs.rs#711)        Some(($($values,)*)).filter(|_| !$carry)
[712](https://docs.rs#712)    };
[713](https://docs.rs#713)    (
[714](https://docs.rs#714)        $this:ident,
[715](https://docs.rs#715)        $advance:ident,
[716](https://docs.rs#716)        $reset:ident,
[717](https://docs.rs#717)        $carry:ident
[718](https://docs.rs#718)        @ $($values:expr,)*
[719](https://docs.rs#719)        @ $ty:ident, $($types:ident,)*
[720](https://docs.rs#720)        @ $($placeholders:pat,)*
[721](https://docs.rs#721)    ) => {{
[722](https://docs.rs#722)        let (.., item, $($placeholders,)*) = $this;
[723](https://docs.rs#723)        let (x, new_carry) = if $carry {
[724](https://docs.rs#724)            match Sequence::$advance(item) {
[725](https://docs.rs#725)                Some(x) => (x, false),
[726](https://docs.rs#726)                None => (Sequence::$reset()?, true),
[727](https://docs.rs#727)            }
[728](https://docs.rs#728)        } else {
[729](https://docs.rs#729)            (item.clone(), false)
[730](https://docs.rs#730)        };
[731](https://docs.rs#731)        impl_seq_advance_for_tuple!(
[732](https://docs.rs#732)            $this,
[733](https://docs.rs#733)            $advance,
[734](https://docs.rs#734)            $reset,
[735](https://docs.rs#735)            new_carry
[736](https://docs.rs#736)            @ x, $($values,)*
[737](https://docs.rs#737)            @ $($types,)*
[738](https://docs.rs#738)            @ _, $($placeholders,)*
[739](https://docs.rs#739)        )
[740](https://docs.rs#740)    }};
[741](https://docs.rs#741)    ($this:ident, $advance:ident, $reset:ident @ $($types:ident,)*) => {{
[742](https://docs.rs#742)        let (.., item) = $this;
[743](https://docs.rs#743)        let (x, carry) = match Sequence::$advance(item) {
[744](https://docs.rs#744)            Some(x) => (x, false),
[745](https://docs.rs#745)            None => (Sequence::$reset()?, true),
[746](https://docs.rs#746)        };
[747](https://docs.rs#747)        impl_seq_advance_for_tuple!($this, $advance, $reset, carry @ x, @ $($types,)* @ _,)
[748](https://docs.rs#748)    }};
[749](https://docs.rs#749)}

[751](https://docs.rs#751)macro_rules! impl_sequence_for_tuple {
[752](https://docs.rs#752)    ($($types:ident,)* @ $last:ident) => {
[753](https://docs.rs#753)        impl<$($types,)* $last> Sequence for ($($types,)* $last,)
[754](https://docs.rs#754)        where
[755](https://docs.rs#755)            $($types: Sequence + Clone,)*
[756](https://docs.rs#756)            $last: Sequence,
[757](https://docs.rs#757)        {
[758](https://docs.rs#758)            const CARDINALITY: usize =
[759](https://docs.rs#759)                $(<$types as Sequence>::CARDINALITY *)* <$last as Sequence>::CARDINALITY;
[760](https://docs.rs#760)
[761](https://docs.rs#761)            fn next(&self) -> Option<Self> {
[762](https://docs.rs#762)                impl_seq_advance_for_tuple!(self, next, first @ $($types,)*)
[763](https://docs.rs#763)            }
[764](https://docs.rs#764)
[765](https://docs.rs#765)            fn previous(&self) -> Option<Self> {
[766](https://docs.rs#766)                impl_seq_advance_for_tuple!(self, previous, last @ $($types,)*)
[767](https://docs.rs#767)            }
[768](https://docs.rs#768)
[769](https://docs.rs#769)            fn first() -> Option<Self> {
[770](https://docs.rs#770)                Some((
[771](https://docs.rs#771)                    $(<$types as Sequence>::first()?,)*
[772](https://docs.rs#772)                    <$last as Sequence>::first()?,
[773](https://docs.rs#773)                ))
[774](https://docs.rs#774)            }
[775](https://docs.rs#775)
[776](https://docs.rs#776)            fn last() -> Option<Self> {
[777](https://docs.rs#777)                Some((
[778](https://docs.rs#778)                    $(<$types as Sequence>::last()?,)*
[779](https://docs.rs#779)                    <$last as Sequence>::last()?,
[780](https://docs.rs#780)                ))
[781](https://docs.rs#781)            }
[782](https://docs.rs#782)        }
[783](https://docs.rs#783)    };
[784](https://docs.rs#784)}

# Sequence in enum_iterator - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/enum-iterator/2.3.0/enum_iterator/trait.Sequence.html

`pub trait Sequence: `[Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sized.html) {
    const [CARDINALITY](https://docs.rs#associatedconstant.CARDINALITY): [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.usize.html);
    // Required methods
    fn [next](https://docs.rs#tymethod.next)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<Self>;
[previous](https://docs.rs#tymethod.previous)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<Self>;
[first](https://docs.rs#tymethod.first)() -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<Self>;
[last](https://docs.rs#tymethod.last)() -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<Self>;
}## Expand description

Trait to iterate over the values of a type.

The [crate root](https://docs.rs/index.html) defines useful functions to work with types implementing `Sequence`.

[§](https://docs.rs#derivation)Derivation

`Sequence` can be derived for `enum` and `struct` types. Specifically, it can be derived
for:

- Enumerations whose variants meet one of the following criteria:
- The variant does not have fields.
- The variant has fields meeting all these conditions:
- Every field has a type that implements `Sequence`.
- Every field but the last one has a type that implements `Clone`.

- Every field has a type that implements

- Enumerations without variants.
- Structures whose fields meet all these conditions:
- Every field has a type that implements `Sequence`.
- Every field but the last one has a type that implements `Clone`.

- Every field has a type that implements
- Unit structures (i.e. without fields).

The cardinality (number of values) of the type must not exceed `usize::MAX`.

[§](https://docs.rs#laws)Laws

`T: Sequence` implies the following assertions:

- `T::first().and_then(|x| x.previous()).is_none()`
- `T::last().and_then(|x| x.next()).is_none()`
- `T::first().is_none()`⇔- `T::last().is_none()`
- `std::iter::successors(T::first(), T::next)`must eventually yield- `T::last()`.
- If `T`is inhabited,`T::first().is_some()`.

If a manual implementation of `Sequence` violates any of these laws, the functions at the crate root may misbehave, including panicking.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

[§](https://docs.rs#c-like-enumeration)C-like enumeration

```
use enum_iterator::{all, cardinality, Sequence};
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Sequence)]
enum Direction { North, South, West, East }
assert_eq!(cardinality::<Direction>(), 4);
assert_eq!(all::<Direction>().collect::<Vec<_>>(), [
    Direction::North,
    Direction::South,
    Direction::West,
    Direction::East,
]);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#enumeration-with-data)Enumeration with data

```
use enum_iterator::{all, cardinality, Sequence};
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Sequence)]
enum Direction { North, South, West, East }
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Sequence)]
enum Greeting {
    Hi,
    Bye,
}
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Sequence)]
enum Action {
    Move(Direction),
    Jump,
    Talk { greeting: Greeting, loud: bool },
}
assert_eq!(cardinality::<Action>(), 4 + 1 + 2 * 2);
assert_eq!(all::<Action>().collect::<Vec<_>>(), [
    Action::Move(Direction::North),
    Action::Move(Direction::South),
    Action::Move(Direction::West),
    Action::Move(Direction::East),
    Action::Jump,
    Action::Talk { greeting: Greeting::Hi, loud: false },
    Action::Talk { greeting: Greeting::Hi, loud: true },
    Action::Talk { greeting: Greeting::Bye, loud: false },
    Action::Talk { greeting: Greeting::Bye, loud: true },
]);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#structure)Structure

```
use enum_iterator::{all, cardinality, Sequence};
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Sequence)]
enum Side {
    Left,
    Right,
}
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Sequence)]
enum LimbKind {
    Arm,
    Leg,
}
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Sequence)]
struct Limb {
    kind: LimbKind,
    side: Side,
}
assert_eq!(cardinality::<Limb>(), 4);
assert_eq!(all::<Limb>().collect::<Vec<_>>(), [
    Limb { kind: LimbKind::Arm, side: Side::Left },
    Limb { kind: LimbKind::Arm, side: Side::Right },
    Limb { kind: LimbKind::Leg, side: Side::Left },
    Limb { kind: LimbKind::Leg, side: Side::Right },
]);
```
## Required Associated Constants[§](https://docs.rs#required-associated-consts)

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

Returns value following `*self` or `None` if this was the end.

Values are yielded in the following order. Comparisons between values are based on their
relative order as yielded by `next`; an element yielded after another is considered greater.

- For primitive types, in increasing order (same as `Ord`).
- For arrays and tuples, in lexicographic order of the sequence of their elements.
- When derived for an enumeration, in variant definition order.
- When derived for a structure, in lexicographic order of the sequence of its fields taken in definition order.

The order described above is the same as `Ord` if any custom `Sequence` implementation
follows `Ord` and any enumeration has its variants defined in increasing order of
discriminant.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-1)Example

```
use enum_iterator::Sequence;
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Sequence)]
enum Day { Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday }
assert_eq!(Day::Tuesday.next(), Some(Day::Wednesday));
```
Returns value preceding `*self` or `None` if this was the beginning.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-2)Example

```
use enum_iterator::Sequence;
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Sequence)]
enum Day { Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday }
assert_eq!(Day::Wednesday.previous(), Some(Day::Tuesday));
```

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety", so this trait is not object safe.*

# all in enum_iterator - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/enum-iterator/2.3.0/enum_iterator/fn.all.html

## Expand description

Returns an iterator over all values of type `T`.

Values are yielded in the order defined by [ Sequence::next](https://docs.rs/trait.Sequence.html#tymethod.next), starting with

[.](https://docs.rs/trait.Sequence.html#tymethod.first)

`Sequence::first`[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use enum_iterator::{all, Sequence};
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Sequence)]
enum Color { Red, Green, Blue }
assert_eq!(
    all::<Color>().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
    [Color::Red, Color::Green, Color::Blue],
);
```

---

use enum_iterator::{cardinality, Sequence};
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Sequence)]
enum Color { Red, Green, Blue }
assert_eq!(cardinality::<Color>(), 3);

# first in enum_iterator - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/enum-iterator/2.3.0/enum_iterator/fn.first.html

## Expand description

Returns the first value of type `T`.

Same as [ Sequence::first](https://docs.rs/trait.Sequence.html#tymethod.first).

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use enum_iterator::{first, Sequence};
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Sequence)]
enum Day { Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday }
assert_eq!(first::<Day>(), Some(Day::Monday));
```

# next in enum_iterator - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/enum-iterator/2.3.0/enum_iterator/fn.next.html

## Expand description

Returns the next value of type `T` or `None` if this was the end.

Same as [ Sequence::next](https://docs.rs/trait.Sequence.html#tymethod.next).

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use enum_iterator::{next, Sequence};
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Sequence)]
enum Day { Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday }
assert_eq!(next(&Day::Friday), Some(Day::Saturday));
```

# reverse_all in enum_iterator - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/enum-iterator/2.3.0/enum_iterator/fn.reverse_all.html

# Function reverse_all

## Expand description

use enum_iterator::{reverse_all, Sequence};
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Sequence)]

    reverse_all::<Color>().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
    [Color::Blue, Color::Green, Color::Red],
);

# enum_iterator - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/enum-iterator/latest/enum_iterator/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#overview)Overview

Tools to iterate over the values of a type.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use enum_iterator::{all, cardinality, first, last, next, previous, reverse_all, Sequence};
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Sequence)]
enum Day { Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday }
assert_eq!(cardinality::<Day>(), 7);
assert_eq!(all::<Day>().collect::<Vec<_>>(), [
    Day::Monday,
    Day::Tuesday,
    Day::Wednesday,
    Day::Thursday,
    Day::Friday,
    Day::Saturday,
    Day::Sunday,
]);
assert_eq!(first::<Day>(), Some(Day::Monday));
assert_eq!(last::<Day>(), Some(Day::Sunday));
assert_eq!(next(&Day::Tuesday), Some(Day::Wednesday));
assert_eq!(previous(&Day::Wednesday), Some(Day::Tuesday));
assert_eq!(reverse_all::<Day>().collect::<Vec<_>>(), [
    Day::Sunday,
    Day::Saturday,
    Day::Friday,
    Day::Thursday,
    Day::Wednesday,
    Day::Tuesday,
    Day::Monday,
]);
```
```
use enum_iterator::{cardinality, first, last, Sequence};
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Sequence)]
struct Foo {
    a: bool,
    b: u8,
}
assert_eq!(cardinality::<Foo>(), 512);
assert_eq!(first::<Foo>(), Some(Foo { a: false, b: 0 }));
assert_eq!(last::<Foo>(), Some(Foo { a: true, b: 255 }));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#custom-crate-path-in-generated-code)Custom crate path in generated code

The code generated by the derive macro defaults to using `::enum_iterator` as the path for
items defined in this crate. This can be customized using the
`#[enum_iterator(crate = foo::bar)]` derive macro attribute.

```
#[derive(enum_iterator::Sequence)]
#[enum_iterator(crate = enum_iterator)]
struct Foo;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#rust-version)Rust version

This crate tracks stable Rust. Minor releases may require a newer Rust version. Patch releases must not require a newer Rust version.

[§](https://docs.rs#contribute)Contribute

All contributions shall be licensed under the [0BSD license](https://spdx.org/licenses/0BSD.html).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [All](https://docs.rs/struct.All.html)
- Iterator over the values of type `T`.
- [Reverse](https://docs.rs/struct.ReverseAll.html)- All
- Iterator over the values of type `T`in reverse order.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Sequence](https://docs.rs/trait.Sequence.html)
- Trait to iterate over the values of a type.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [all](https://docs.rs/fn.all.html)
- Returns an iterator over all values of type `T`.
- [cardinality](https://docs.rs/fn.cardinality.html)
- Returns the cardinality (number of values) of `T`
- [first](https://docs.rs/fn.first.html)
- Returns the first value of type `T`.
- [last](https://docs.rs/fn.last.html)
- Returns the last value of type `T`.
- [next](https://docs.rs/fn.next.html)
- Returns the next value of type `T`or`None`if this was the end.
- [next_](https://docs.rs/fn.next_cycle.html)- cycle
- Returns the next value of type `T`or`first()`
- [previous](https://docs.rs/fn.previous.html)
- Returns the previous value of type `T`or`None`if this was the beginning.
- [previous_](https://docs.rs/fn.previous_cycle.html)- cycle
- Returns the previous value of type `T`or`last()`
- [reverse_](https://docs.rs/fn.reverse_all.html)- all
- Returns an iterator over all values of type `T`in the reverse order of`all`

## Derive Macros[§](https://docs.rs#derives)

- [Sequence](https://docs.rs/derive.Sequence.html)
- Derives `Sequence`.

All the builds on docs.rs are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The limits for this crate are the following:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                    If a build fails because it hit one of those limits please
                    [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                    to get them increased.

use enum_iterator::{all, cardinality, first, last, next, previous, reverse_all, Sequence};
enum Day { Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday }

# proc_macro2 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/^1.0.39/

## Expand description

A wrapper around the procedural macro API of the compiler’s [ proc_macro](https://doc.rust-lang.org/proc_macro/index.html)
crate. This library serves two purposes:

-
**Bring proc-macro-like functionality to other contexts like build.rs and main.rs.**Types from`proc_macro`are entirely specific to procedural macros and cannot ever exist in code outside of a procedural macro. Meanwhile`proc_macro2`types may exist anywhere including non-macro code. By developing foundational libraries like[syn](https://github.com/dtolnay/syn)and[quote](https://github.com/dtolnay/quote)against`proc_macro2`rather than`proc_macro`, the procedural macro ecosystem becomes easily applicable to many other use cases and we avoid reimplementing non-macro equivalents of those libraries.
-
**Make procedural macros unit testable.**As a consequence of being specific to procedural macros, nothing that uses`proc_macro`can be executed from a unit test. In order for helper libraries or components of a macro to be testable in isolation, they must be implemented using`proc_macro2`.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

The skeleton of a typical procedural macro typically looks like this:

```
extern crate proc_macro;
#[proc_macro_derive(MyDerive)]
pub fn my_derive(input: proc_macro::TokenStream) -> proc_macro::TokenStream {
    let input = proc_macro2::TokenStream::from(input);
    let output: proc_macro2::TokenStream = {
        /* transform input */
    };
    proc_macro::TokenStream::from(output)
}
```
If parsing with [Syn](https://github.com/dtolnay/syn), you’ll use [ parse_macro_input!](https://docs.rs/syn/2.0/syn/macro.parse_macro_input.html) instead to
propagate parse errors correctly back to the compiler when parsing fails.

[§](https://docs.rs#unstable-features)Unstable features

The default feature set of proc-macro2 tracks the most recent stable
compiler API. Functionality in `proc_macro` that is not yet stable is not
exposed by proc-macro2 by default.

To opt into the additional APIs available in the most recent nightly
compiler, the `procmacro2_semver_exempt` config flag must be passed to
rustc. We will polyfill those nightly-only APIs back to Rust 1.68.0. As
these are unstable APIs that track the nightly compiler, minor versions of
proc-macro2 may make breaking changes to them at any time.

`RUSTFLAGS='--cfg procmacro2_semver_exempt' cargo build`Note that this must not only be done for your crate, but for any crate that depends on your crate. This infectious nature is intentional, as it serves as a reminder that you are outside of the normal semver guarantees.

Semver exempt methods are marked as such in the proc-macro2 documentation.

[§](https://docs.rs#thread-safety)Thread-Safety

Most types in this crate are `!Sync` because the underlying compiler
types make use of thread-local memory, meaning they cannot be accessed from
a different thread.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [extra](https://docs.rs/extra/index.html)
- Items which do not have a correspondence to any API in the proc_macro crate, but are necessary to include in proc-macro2.
- [token_](https://docs.rs/token_stream/index.html)- stream
- Public implementation details for the `TokenStream`type, such as iterators.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Group](https://docs.rs/struct.Group.html)
- A delimited token stream.
- [Ident](https://docs.rs/struct.Ident.html)
- A word of Rust code, which may be a keyword or legal variable name.
- [LexError](https://docs.rs/struct.LexError.html)
- Error returned from `TokenStream::from_str`.
- [Line](https://docs.rs/struct.LineColumn.html)- Column - `span-locations`
- A line-column pair representing the start or end of a `Span`.
- [Literal](https://docs.rs/struct.Literal.html)
- A literal string (`"hello"`), byte string (`b"hello"`), character (`'a'`), byte character (`b'a'`), an integer or floating point number with or without a suffix (`1`,`1u8`,`2.3`,`2.3f32`).
- [Punct](https://docs.rs/struct.Punct.html)
- A `Punct`is a single punctuation character like`+`,`-`or`#`.
- [Span](https://docs.rs/struct.Span.html)
- A region of source code, along with macro expansion information.
- [Token](https://docs.rs/struct.TokenStream.html)- Stream
- An abstract stream of tokens, or more concretely a sequence of token trees.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Conversion](https://docs.rs/enum.ConversionErrorKind.html)- Error - Kind - `procmacro2_semver_exempt`
- Error when retrieving a string literal’s unescaped value.
- [Delimiter](https://docs.rs/enum.Delimiter.html)
- Describes how a sequence of token trees is delimited.
- [Escape](https://docs.rs/enum.EscapeError.html)- Error - `procmacro2_semver_exempt`
- Errors and warnings that can occur during string, char, and byte unescaping.
- [Spacing](https://docs.rs/enum.Spacing.html)
- Whether a `Punct`is followed immediately by another`Punct`or followed by another token or whitespace.
- [Token](https://docs.rs/enum.TokenTree.html)- Tree
- A single token or a delimited sequence of token trees (e.g. `[1, (), ..]`).

# quote - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/quote/^1.0.18/

## Expand description

This crate provides the [ quote!](https://docs.rs/macro.quote.html) macro for turning Rust syntax tree data
structures into tokens of source code.

Procedural macros in Rust receive a stream of tokens as input, execute arbitrary Rust code to determine how to manipulate those tokens, and produce a stream of tokens to hand back to the compiler to compile into the caller’s crate. Quasi-quoting is a solution to one piece of that — producing tokens to return to the compiler.

The idea of quasi-quoting is that we write *code* that we treat as *data*.
Within the `quote!` macro, we can write what looks like code to our text
editor or IDE. We get all the benefits of the editor’s brace matching,
syntax highlighting, indentation, and maybe autocompletion. But rather than
compiling that as code into the current crate, we can treat it as data, pass
it around, mutate it, and eventually hand it back to the compiler as tokens
to compile into the macro caller’s crate.

This crate is motivated by the procedural macro use case, but is a general-purpose Rust quasi-quoting library and is not specific to procedural macros.

```
[dependencies]
quote = "1.0"
```
[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

The following quasi-quoted block of code is something you might find in [a](https://serde.rs/)
procedural macro having to do with data structure serialization. The `#var`
syntax performs interpolation of runtime variables into the quoted tokens.
Check out the documentation of the [ quote!](https://docs.rs/macro.quote.html) macro for more detail about
the syntax. See also the

[macro which is important for implementing hygienic procedural macros.](https://docs.rs/macro.quote_spanned.html)

`quote_spanned!````
let tokens = quote! {
    struct SerializeWith #generics #where_clause {
        value: &'a #field_ty,
        phantom: core::marker::PhantomData<#item_ty>,
    }
    impl #generics serde::Serialize for SerializeWith #generics #where_clause {
        fn serialize<S>(&self, serializer: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error>
        where
            S: serde::Serializer,
        {
            #path(self.value, serializer)
        }
    }
    SerializeWith {
        value: #value,
        phantom: core::marker::PhantomData::<#item_ty>,
    }
};
```
[§](https://docs.rs#non-macro-code-generators)Non-macro code generators

When using `quote` in a build.rs or main.rs and writing the output out to a
file, consider having the code generator pass the tokens through
[prettyplease](https://github.com/dtolnay/prettyplease) before writing. This way if an error occurs in the generated
code it is convenient for a human to read and debug.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [format_](https://docs.rs/macro.format_ident.html)- ident
- Formatting macro for constructing `Ident`s.
- [quote](https://docs.rs/macro.quote.html)
- The whole point.
- [quote_](https://docs.rs/macro.quote_spanned.html)- spanned
- Same as `quote!`, but applies a given span to all tokens originating within the macro invocation.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Ident](https://docs.rs/trait.IdentFragment.html)- Fragment
- Specialized formatting trait used by `format_ident!`.
- [ToTokens](https://docs.rs/trait.ToTokens.html)
- Types that can be interpolated inside a `quote!`invocation.
- [Token](https://docs.rs/trait.TokenStreamExt.html)- Stream - Ext
- TokenStream extension trait with methods for appending tokens.
